catalog_quote: San Andres Creole English permits both complex syllable onsets and syllable codas, e.g. shrang ‘strong’ and likl ‘little’. Stress assignment is variable and largely follows English patterns. There are a certain amount of grammatical, pragmatic and lexical tonal oppositions where rising contrasts with falling tone. I shall give one example of each kind of oppositions with the item with the falling tone mentioned first, the item with the raising tone in second place: kyan ‘can’ vs. kyaan ‘cannot’, no [neg] vs. noo [neg.emph], huol ‘whole’ vs. huol ‘to hold’. No systematic investigation of the tonal oppositions of San Andres Creole English has been conducted so far. Following Marcia Dittman (p.c.), there seem to be tonal oppositions in Providence Creole English.
